Under the direction of a PBOT-MO Environmental Systems Division (ESD) Manager II. Forestry and Parks are responsible for managing our forests, public lands and provincial parks. Our Ministry accountabilities include:

Growing Alberta’s environmentally responsible wood products and forestry sector.
Protecting Alberta’s forests from wildfire.
Preserving our provincial parks for the recreation and enjoyment of Albertans.
Enabling access to public lands for recreation and purposes while prioritizing conservation.
Managing public lands and balancing sustainable rangelands and grazing leases for Alberta producers.

Within the Ministry, Land Operations Division, delivers an integrated approach to the management of provincial Crown Land. The work of the Division reflects the full range of users of the province’s Crown land including conservation, recreation, tourism, energy, forestry, agriculture and traditional land uses.

Role Responsibilities

The Hay-Zama Bison Technician supports senior and area Wildlife and Species at Risk (SAR) Biologists in the delivery of the Wood Bison Conservation and Recovery Program in northwestern Alberta.

This position plays a key role in coordinating and supporting all aspects of the Hay-Zama bison harvest season, including engagement with Indigenous and non-Indigenous harvesters, issuing licenses and registration certificates, collecting and processing disease monitoring samples, and liaising with local communities and stakeholders.

The role also contributes to the implementation of approved recovery actions for Wood Bison, such as population surveys, habitat monitoring, and conflict mitigation measures.

Key Responsibilities

Support the delivery of the Hay-Zama bison harvest season by issuing Indigenous hunter licenses and compulsory registration certificates, collecting and processing biological samples for disease monitoring, and providing information and coordination support to harvesters.
Conduct and assist with wildlife surveys, data collection, and field monitoring activities (ground-based and aerial).
Compile, organize, and manage biological data for entry into the Fish and Wildlife Management Information System (FWMIS).
Support human-bison conflict management and safety awareness initiatives.
Collaborate with Dene Tha’ First Nation partners, Indigenous communities, and municipal stakeholders to advance bison conservation and recovery objectives.

The Job Description is provided for Further details on this position.

APS Compentencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: Understands how individual actions and data collection contribute to broader conservation outcomes. Anticipates long-term implications and adjusts work to support program goals.

Agility: Adapts effectively to changing priorities, field conditions, and timelines. Maintains composure and initiative in dynamic work environments.
Drive for Results: Takes responsibility for delivering quality outcomes and meeting commitments. Seeks feedback and applies learning to improve performance.

Two-year completed diploma in Natural Resources Technology, Environmental Science, Wildlife Management, or a closely related field.
Valid Driver’s License (Class 5).

Current First Aid certification (CPR Level C).
Experience in wildlife or natural resource fieldwork, including data collection, sampling, and monitoring.
Experience using GPS, GIS (ArcGIS), and data management tools for recording and analyzing field data.
Experience preparing technical summaries, reports, or database entries related to wildlife or environmental programs.
Experience participating in aerial or ground-based wildlife surveys is considered an asset.
Experience operating field equipment such as 4x4 vehicles, ATVs, and boats in remote or rugged environments.

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Wetland Delineator/Environmental Scientist for our Cincinnati, Columbus, Cleveland, Dayton, Akron, Toledo or other regional offices.

Your Impact

Assist with planning and execution of wetland delineations and stream assessments for linear and renewable energy projects in the Midwest.
Perform duties as a wetland field team lead in accordance with current USACE 1987 Manual and Regional Supplements. Potential to support other natural resource surveys as needed.
Understand how to operate a GPS unit to collect field data, map habitat types and sensitive resources.
Support preparation of field equipment, mapping, Safe Work Plans, and logistics for field work.
Perform data entry, data analysis and report compilation.
Assist with various governmental agency coordination (USFWS, USACE, EPA, etc.).
Assist and lead preparation of wetland delineation reports, and permit applications for federal and/or state environmental permits, including USACE Section 404 and Section 10, state wetland and stream permits, NPDES, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service coordination, and state natural heritage agency coordination.

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/ .

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here .

Natural Resources And Lands Management Division

The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on SFPUC lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations.

About The Moccasin Planning And Compliance Section Of NRLM

The Moccasin Planning and Compliance (MPC) team is responsible for environmental review and permitting for the eastern division of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System and Hetch Hetchy Water and Power (HHWP), an operating division operating water, wastewater, and power infrastructure across the Sierra Nevada to the Bay Area.

Working Relationships

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams.

The position requires effective communication, sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to develop productive working relationships with individuals who may have different technical expertise, responsibilities, priorities, or perspectives.

Role Location:

There is currently one position available with the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division of the Water Enterprise. The position is located in Moccasin, California and the reporting location is in Moccasin, CA
(located 140 miles east of the San Francisco Bay Area
, requiring a 5-hour round trip commute from the San Francisco Bay Area, by car in fair weather).

Working Location:

The nature of the work may require working in remote field settings, including watersheds, streams, rivers, reservoirs, and federal lands. Duties may require driving or hiking to remote locations using unimproved dirt or mountain roads and working outdoors in inclement weather.

Role Description

Role Description:

The Environmental Planner performs complex environmental planning, permitting, compliance, and lands management work supporting operational and Capital Improvement Program activities of the SFPUC Water Enterprise, including CEQA/NEPA environmental review, Chapter 31 implementation, resource-agency permitting, environmental construction compliance, professional-services administration, federal-land coordination, natural and cultural resources management, Tribal engagement, and strategic program development.

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams. The incumbent develops project descriptions; evaluates environmental impacts and mitigation measures; prepares, manages, and reviews technical studies and regulatory documentation; supports professional services contract administration; coordinates multidisciplinary project teams; and provides technical guidance regarding environmental review, permitting, and regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Analyzes proposed project activities to determine environmental review, documentation, consultation, and permitting requirements, identifies environmental and regulatory risks, and recommends avoidance measures, mitigation measures, and best management practices to minimize environmental impacts and regulatory risk.
Applies and interprets federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, permits, agreements, authorizations, and SFPUC policies, including the Raker Act.

gas health impacts, and more.

The Regulatory Toxicology Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The purpose of this workgroup is to (1) provide statewide consultation to the department's environmental programs other state agencies federal agencies (US EPA, ATSDR) local public health departments, and the general public and (2) conduct public health assessment to identify potential impacts from environmental chemical exposures. The Emerging Issues Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. We currently have an opportunity for an Environmental Engineer

Responsibilities

Reynolds Consumer Products is seeking an Environmental Engineer
to lead environmental compliance and sustainability initiatives at our Louisville
manufacturing facility. This role serves as the site's environmental subject matter expert and is responsible for maintaining regulatory compliance, identifying and managing environmental risk, and partnering with site leadership to support responsible and efficient manufacturing operations.

You Will Have the Opportunity to Make Great Things Happen!

Environmental Compliance

Lead site environmental compliance programs related to air emissions and permits, wastewater, stormwater, hazardous and universal waste, spill prevention, and chemical management.
Maintain the site's environmental compliance calendar and ensure required inspections, monitoring, sampling, reporting, and recordkeeping activities are completed accurately and on time.
Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and corporate environmental requirements, including relevant Kentucky and Louisville requirements.
Manage air compliance activities, including permit-condition tracking, emissions calculations, emissions inventories, VOC reporting, and evaluation of operational changes.

Waste Management

Oversee hazardous, nonhazardous, and universal waste activities, including waste characterization, labeling, storage, inspections, manifests, vendor coordination, and disposal documentation.

Environmental Reporting & Regulatory Affairs

Prepare and submit applicable environmental reports, permit applications, and regulatory filings, including EPCRA, Tier II, TRI/Form R, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, and spill-related requirements.
Serve as the primary site contact for environmental regulatory agencies and support inspections, information requests, permitting activities, and resolution of compliance findings.

Environmental Risk & Corrective Action

Investigate spills, releases, permit deviations, exceedances, and other environmental concerns; identify root causes and ensure corrective actions are completed and effective.
Conduct environmental audits, inspections, and risk assessments; track findings and corrective actions through closure.

Operations & Engineering Partnership

Partner with operations, maintenance, engineering, and site leadership to integrate environmental requirements into day-to-day manufacturing activities.
Participate in Management of Change, capital-project, and process-change reviews to evaluate environmental impacts and permitting requirements before implementation.

Performance & Sustainability

Develop, analyze, and communicate environmental performance metrics, compliance risks, and improvement priorities to site and business-unit leadership.
Drive waste reduction, recycling, resource conservation, sustainability, and other continuous improvement initiatives.

Training & External Resources

Develop and deliver environmental training and provide technical guidance to employees and leaders.
Manage environmental consultants, laboratories, waste vendors, and other third-party service providers as needed.

You Will Love It Here If…

You listen, learn, and evolve
You thrive in a fast-paced environment
You put safety first, always
You are passionate about collaboration, teamwork, and achieving shared goals
You believe in treating all people with respect, operating ethically, and growing a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace
You are committed to improving our impact on local communities and creating positive experiences

Qualifications

Education/Experience

Required

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience to successfully perform the essential functions of the position.
2-4 years of environmental compliance experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.

Preferred

PE, EIT, CHMM, or similar professional certification.
Experience in consumer products, packaging, paper, foil, plastics, or high-volume manufacturing.
Familiarity with ISO 14001 and sustainability reporting programs

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Working knowledge of RCRA, the Clean Air Act, the Clean Water Act, EPCRA, SPCC, and applicable state and local environmental requirements.
Experience managing air emissions, wastewater, stormwater, hazardous waste, spill-prevention, and environmental reporting programs.
Ability to interpret permits and regulations and translate requirements into practical operating controls.
Experience working directly with regulatory agencies and supporting environmental audits and inspections.
Experience with environmental data management, emissions calculations, compliance calendars, and regulatory recordkeeping.
Demonstrated ability to lead corrective actions, manage projects, and influence cross-functional manufacturing teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, project management, and written and verbal communication skills.

Competencies

Ensures Accountability – Establishes clear expectations and follows through to ensure environmental requirements, corrective actions, and commitments are achieved.
Action Oriented – Acts decisively to address environmental risks, compliance gaps, and operational opportunities.
Collaborates – Builds effective partnerships across operations, maintenance, engineering, and leadership to achieve environmental and business objectives.
Communicates Effectively – Conveys technical, regulatory, and environmental information clearly to employees, leaders, and external stakeholders.
Plans and Aligns – Organizes environmental priorities, projects, and compliance activities to meet regulatory and operational requirements.
Technical Learning – Applies and expands environmental expertise to address evolving regulations, manufacturing challenges, and sustainability opportunities.
